headline: Bitcoin ETF outflows near $5B for November as BTC breaks below $60K on tariff fears
summary: A brutal day across crypto: Bitcoin fell 3.6% to $59,780, breaking back below $60,000 as spot ETF outflows for November approached $5 billion — the worst monthly redemption total on record. Renewed tariff concerns from Washington erased the brief optimism from Monday's Nvidia-driven rally, sending liquidations tripling and dragging nearly every major asset lower. Ethereum dropped 5%, Solana fell nearly 7%, and the Fear & Greed index sat at 11 — deep in Extreme Fear territory.

winners.name: Spiko Amundi Overnight Swap Fund (EUR)
winners.catalyst: Spiko's EUR-denominated overnight swap fund posted a modest gain as investors rotated into stable, yield-bearing tokenized assets amid broad crypto market weakness. The fund's near-zero volatility profile made it a relative safe haven on a day when Fear & Greed sat at 11.

losers.name: Zcash
losers.catalyst: Zcash suffered the steepest decline in the top 15, likely amplified by broad market selling pressure and a risk-off environment driven by record Bitcoin ETF outflows and tariff concerns re-entering the macro picture. No specific Zcash catalyst was identified; the move appears to reflect outsized sensitivity to the broader downturn.

whyItMoved:
Two forces collided today to push crypto into its sharpest single-day drop in weeks. First, spot Bitcoin ETF outflows — the funds that allow traditional investors to hold BTC without touching a crypto exchange — hit another $570 million in net redemptions, bringing November's running total close to $5 billion. That is the worst monthly outflow figure since these funds launched in January 2024, and it reflects sustained institutional selling rather than a one-day blip. Bitcoin had briefly recovered above $60,000 on Monday, lifted by enthusiasm around Nvidia's earnings, but that recovery evaporated quickly.

The second force was macro: renewed tariff concerns out of Washington revived the kind of risk-off sentiment that tends to hit speculative assets hard. When investors pull back from risk broadly, crypto tends to move faster and further than equities — and that pattern held today. Liquidations tripled compared to the prior session as leveraged long positions were forcibly closed, amplifying the downward move.

The result was a broad selloff with almost no shelter. Ethereum fell 5%, Solana dropped nearly 7%, and Hyperliquid slid 7.35%. Zcash led losses at -14.74%, though no Zcash-specific news drove that move — it appears to reflect the asset's higher sensitivity to broad market swings. The one exception was Spiko's EUR-denominated tokenized fund, which edged up 0.77% as a small amount of capital rotated toward yield-bearing, low-volatility instruments. The Fear & Greed index at 11 — deep in Extreme Fear — captures the session's tone accurately.
worthKnowing: South Korea proposed lifting its 2017 ban on initial coin offerings (ICOs — fundraising events where new crypto tokens are sold to the public), a move that would open one of Asia's largest economies to onshore token issuances for the first time in nearly a decade.

BlackRock expanded its tokenized money market fund — which holds $100 million in assets — to investors in Hong Kong, continuing the firm's push into real-world asset tokenization despite the broader market downturn.
Prominent crypto trader Ansem's wallet was reportedly drained of $2.57 million, triggering a 55% crash in his associated creator token; Ansem denied involvement, suggesting the wallet was hacked.
